summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of Crohn’s disease status post subtotal colectomy, was admitted with fever and abdominal pain 36 hours after a social outing. He had recently been discharged from a prior admission with increased immunosuppression. Evaluation revealed an acute flare of Crohn’s disease confirmed by flexible sigmoidoscopy and biopsy, showing ulceration and inflammation at the ileosigmoid anastomosis. His elevated creatinine of 1.6 improved to 1.2 with IV hydration, resolving acute kidney injury. An 8mm nonobstructing kidney stone was found on renal ultrasound, contributing to his pain. He was treated with IV steroids, transitioned to oral prednisone, and given a course of ciprofloxacin due to fever in the setting of immunosuppression. The pain service initiated a PCA and started Flexeril, later transitioning to a short outpatient opioid supply. He tolerated a regular diet, and his symptoms improved. He was discharged home with follow-up arranged and instructions to monitor for worsening symptoms.
problems: Adrenal cortical steroids causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
